simple.meaning: הָסָה (hâçâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to hush.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 8 times in Numbers, Judges, Nehemiah, Amos, Habakkuk, and 2 more, beginning at Numbers 13:30. The surrounding contexts include family line, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הָסָה (H2013) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: הָסָה (hâçâh) / H2013 is traced through Numbers 13:30, Judges 3:19, Nehemiah 8:11, Amos 6:10 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, “Let’s go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it!”

timeline.evidenceText: Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, “Let’s go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it!”
But he himself turned back from the stone idols that were by Gilgal, and said, “I have a secret message for you, O king.”
So the Levites calmed all the people, saying, “Hold your peace, for the day is holy. Don’t be grieved.”

“When a man’s relative carries him, even he who burns him, to bring bodies out of the house, and asks him who is in the innermost parts of the house, ‘Is there yet any with you?’ And he says, ‘No;’ then he will say, ‘Hush! Indeed we must not mention Yahweh’s name.’
The songs of the temple will be wailing in that day,” says the Lord Yahweh.
But Yahweh is in his holy temple. Let all the earth be silent before him!”
Be silent at the presence of the Lord† The word translated “Lord” is “Adonai.” Yahweh, for the day of Yahweh is at hand. For Yahweh has prepared a sacrifice. He has consecrated his guests.

structuredEvidence.canonicalTrailSummary: The occurrence trail begins at Numbers 13:30 and continues through Zechariah 2:17.

definitions.usage: hold peace (tongue), (keep) silence, be silent, still.
definitions.full: H2013. has הָ֑ס הַס, interjection hush! keep silence (probably onomatopoetic) Judg 3:19 and he said, I have a secret errand unto thee, O king, הָ֔ס וַיּאֹמֶר and he said, Keep silence! Amos 6:10 הָ֔ס וְאָמַר (while burying men in a pestilence), 8:3 (elliptical) in every place: הָֽס הִשְׁלִיךְ they cast them (the corpses) forth, (saying) Hysh ! followed by י מִמְּנֵי ׳(מִמָּנָיו) Hab 2:20 ; Zeph 1:7 ; Zechariah 2:17. Inflected, as though a verb, imperative plural הַ֔סּוּ Neh 8:11 (Ges compares Arabic [= הֲלֹם ] hither! inflected as an imperative, e.g. , : W AG i. § 368 ). Hence as denominative Hiph`il imperfect with apocope וַיַּ֫הַס Num 13:30 and Caleb stilled the people. הֲפֻגָה see below פוג .
